patch_description:
This design replaces the independently parameterized rotation layers and linear CZ chain with a parameter-shared, multiscale phase-echo circuit.

The dense IsingZZ feature map already supplies data-dependent all-to-all entanglement, so the ansatz uses a sparse three-stage hypercube scaffold rather than duplicating dense interactions. Each CZ stage is a disjoint perfect matching along one hypercube dimension. Interleaved noncommuting RY and RX layers repeatedly convert encoded phases into measurable populations while spreading correlations across all eight qubits.

Qubits are divided into the two checkerboard partitions of the hypercube. Parameters are shared within each partition, creating two regularized processing channels instead of eight independent channels. A globally shared bridge rotation couples their representations. This reduces the ansatz from 24 to 7 parameters per block, and from 146 to 44 total trainable parameters. The final layer uses RX rather than RZ so its parameters remain directly relevant to the fixed Z readout, including in the final block.
